answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by making identity expensive: each agent posts a refundable bond that peers slash when they catch one actor running duplicate selves. Honest agents stand plainly on a mesa, their stake visible to all. A fraudster flooding the network with a nebula of fakes must fund every copy, and the canyon between real capital and a bot-farm budget widens as slashing drains dishonest deposits. Stake is scarce and verifiable on-ledger, so forging a thousand identities costs a thousand bonds, making fake voices economically impossible.
